wiki-iran.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Iran, and a daily count of how many people open it. It is a rough gauge of how many ordinary readers are looking up the country's history, geography and government rather than following a specific news story.
wiki-iran.recent: US and Iranian forces traded strikes through late August and early September, with mines stopping a supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz and the UAE intercepting a drone. Tehran is now weighing transit fees on Hormuz, Houthi fighters have taken Perim Island at Bab al-Mandab, and Iranian strikes damaged eight F-15s at a Jordanian base.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet crude from the North Sea, settled in dollars and used to price roughly two-thirds of the world's traded oil. Refiners, airlines and finance ministries all set their budgets against it.
brent.recent: Three export routes closed at once: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha and the Red Sea coast, then Perim Island at Bab al-Mandab, while drones launched from Maysan in Iraq struck the East–West pipeline Saudi Arabia built precisely to bypass Hormuz. Tehran is now weighing transit fees for Hormuz itself. The war reached US consumer prices, which rose 0.4% in August.

wti.standing: The US benchmark grade of light, sweet crude, priced at the Cushing, Oklahoma tank farm where American pipelines converge. It sets what US refiners pay, and pump prices and airline fuel costs follow it within weeks.
wti.recent: A US-Iran war closed in on the barrel itself: three tankers turned back at Hormuz without a shot fired, Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone there, explosions hit the Kharg export island, and Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha to complete their hold on the Red Sea coast. Argus puts exports down 7 million barrels a day.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for a million British thermal units of natural gas, settled at a delivery point in Louisiana where several interstate pipelines meet. It sets the fuel cost of American power generation and the floor under US LNG cargoes sold abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The domestic price stayed loose while the fuel got scarcer everywhere else: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour with EU storage near 64%, Bangladesh committed to two new LNG terminals by 2030, and Ukraine struck a gas plant at Novy Urengoy 1,700 miles inside Russia.

wheat.standing: The IMF's global wheat benchmark, a dollar-per-tonne average of export prices for the world's most widely traded food grain. It sets what flour millers pay, and bread subsidies in importing countries are budgeted against it.
wheat.recent: The UN's food agency logged a third straight monthly rise in its price index, to 133.3 points, with cereals among the drivers, and named conflict and extreme weather as the cause. Europe's drought took France's maize harvest to a four-decade low, and forecasters warned of an El Nino that could be the strongest in decades running into 2027.

rice.standing: The world reference price for a tonne of milled white rice, compiled monthly by the IMF from Asian export quotations. It is the staple calorie for more than half the planet, and import bills across West Africa and the Gulf are written against it.
rice.recent: The UN food agency's index rose for a third month to 133.3 points on conflict and extreme weather, but cereals have not carried grain buyers evenly — in Ekiti, Nigeria, farmers walked away from ofada rice after uninsured floods rotted two harvests in the ground. Where staples are imported, the squeeze lands on households: in Tehran, a packet of tea now costs a day's wage.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, transformers and building wire are all claims on it, so its price is the running cost of electrification.
copper.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains the price. What copper appeared in was biology and sabotage: Texas A&M researchers working on how immune cells use copper against bacteria in College Station, and the explosives found on power lines in Saxony, which threatened German grid hardware rather than any supply of the metal.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, set by what buyers pay for it rather than by any official. It is the reference price for mortgages, corporate borrowing and much of the world's sovereign debt.
us-10y.recent: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha on Thursday and oil ran to $105, turning the question in Washington from a cut to a hike. The long end was already selling on term premium rather than the policy rate, and Norway's wealth fund signalled it may drop $80bn of Treasuries.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large companies listed in the United States, covering roughly four-fifths of the value of the American stock market. Most US retirement savings is measured against it.
sp500.recent: Two forces pulled against each other. Global bond yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears, and the August US figures showed rising petrol costs driving a sharp inflation increase, while AI demand kept server sales growing even at higher prices. The dollar fell to its weakest since May after Waller's comments.

nasdaq100.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Software, chipmakers and the big platform firms dominate it, so it moves on the technology cycle more than on the broad economy.
nasdaq100.recent: Apple set the tone for the window's tech news, launching a foldable it calls the iPhone Duo at $1,999 without a standard iPhone 18 beside it — a bet on average selling price after years of flat unit sales, and one that drew a public roasting from Samsung. Elsewhere the platform firms spent on capacity rather than product: Google committed €13 billion to Finnish datacentres, keeping a reactor open to power them.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price a US motorist pays for a gallon of regular gasoline, surveyed weekly across the country. It is the most visible consumer price in the American economy, and roughly half of it is the cost of crude oil.
us-gas-retail.recent: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze while Hormuz stayed closed, and the loss of refining capacity fed straight through to American pumps: the national average passed $4.03 a gallon, above the 2012 record, and diesel hit $5.85. The same war premium is showing up at pumps from Johannesburg to Islamabad.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered at the Title Transfer Facility in the Netherlands, the pricing point most European gas contracts settle against. Industry, power generation and home heating across the continent are billed off it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe went into the refill season short: EU storage sat near 64% with winter approaching, and buyers competed for spot LNG cargoes against Asian demand rather than drawing on tanks they had already filled. Prices topped €75 per megawatt-hour in Amsterdam, and new Asian buyers are locking in long-term supply — Bangladesh is building two import terminals by 2030.

vix.standing: The Cboe Volatility Index, derived from S&P 500 option prices, measuring how much movement traders are paying to hedge over the coming 30 days. It rises when protection gets expensive, which is why it is read as a fear gauge.

fx-pkr.standing: The number of Pakistani rupees one US dollar buys. Pakistan imports its fuel and much of its food in dollars and services external debt in them, so the rate sets both the cost of living and the size of the repayment bill.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's Pakistan news was fiscal rather than monetary: a petroleum levy of 114 rupees a liter that put marchers on the street in Gujranwala, and an ADB digitalisation loan Islamabad approved over its own planners' objections. Neither of those reaches the exchange rate, and nothing in the period's coverage accounts for its movement.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar. Nigeria earns dollars from crude oil and spends them on refined fuel, food and school fees abroad, so the rate sets the price of imported life for 230 million people.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's pilgrimage commission set 26 September as the payment deadline for Hajj, forcing pilgrims to buy riyals nine months before they travel and pushing that demand into one narrow window. Dangote Cement, meanwhile, booked a London investor day rather than raise capital at home, a judgement on how little depth the Lagos market offers.

fx-egp.standing: The number of Egyptian pounds one US dollar buys, set on the interbank market the central bank oversees. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the rate feeds straight into bread and energy costs for a population of over 100 million.
fx-egp.recent: Xi Jinping made his first state visit to Cairo in a decade, meeting Sisi and pressing Middle East states to build their own security framework — Egypt approached it looking for leverage from a weak position. At home the state moved to take over the subsidized fertilizer system, stripping cooperatives in five governorates.

fx-try.standing: The lira's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. Turkey imports nearly all its energy, so the rate sets the cost of the country's fuel and feeds straight into domestic prices.
fx-try.recent: Ankara cut its growth forecast and raised its inflation forecast in the medium-term programme, naming the Gulf war as the cause: a war premium in the oil price arrives in a near-total energy importer as a larger import bill before it arrives as domestic inflation. The US Treasury also sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran dealings.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka against the US dollar. Bangladesh buys nearly all of its fuel and much of its industrial input abroad while earning dollars from garment exports and remittances, so the rate sets the cost of both the energy bill and the import basket.
fx-bdt.recent: The state's dollar bill is being deliberately enlarged: Dhaka committed to two new LNG import terminals by 2030, locking future power generation to a fuel priced in dollars, and took a $1bn Islamic Development Bank facility to expand domestic refining. Both deepen the import exposure the rate has to absorb.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah's price against the US dollar. Indonesia is the world's largest nickel and thermal-coal exporter, so the rate tracks commodity earnings, and it sets the local cost of the fuel and food the archipelago imports.
fx-idr.recent: The Anak Krakatau eruption shut Soekarno-Hatta and stranded 166,000 passengers, a hit to tourism and air freight earnings. Against that, Jakarta ratified a trade pact with Moscow and opened 138 oil and gas blocks to Russian partners, and El Niño-driven peat fires that emitted 76 million tonnes of carbon closed schools across the border in Sarawak.

fx-lbp.standing: The number of Lebanese pounds one US dollar buys. The currency collapsed after 2019 and the country now prices most goods in dollars, so the official rate matters mainly as the peg the central bank defends and the line household savings were wiped out against.
fx-lbp.recent: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh on 6 September, killing seven, and on 11 September the army demolished the Ali al-Taher tunnel network with a blast the US Geological Survey logged as a 4.1 tremor. A Lebanese official source said talks with Israel were unlikely the following week. None of this reached the rate, which the central bank holds flat.

fx-cny.standing: The onshore exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, quoted as yuan per dollar, so a falling number means a stronger yuan. The People's Bank of China sets a daily reference rate and holds trading within a band around it, which makes the level a policy signal as much as a market one.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar so a rising number means a weaker rupee. India imports most of its crude oil in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into domestic fuel and fertiliser costs.
fx-inr.recent: India's statisticians rebased the national accounts, shrinking the prior year's base by 7% and flattering a June-quarter growth print of 7.8% — yet measured in dollars the country slipped to sixth-largest economy, an arithmetic of the exchange rate rather than of output. At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, members discussed linking payment systems, with India offering UPI, which handles over 250 billion transfers a year, as the plumbing.

fx-brl.standing: The number of Brazilian reais one US dollar buys. Brazil is a large commodity exporter with a deep local-currency bond market, so the rate carries both the price of what it ships and foreign willingness to hold its debt.
fx-brl.recent: Brazil's fortnight ran to legal and electoral risk rather than anything that reaches the exchange rate: police opened a probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing, Washington listed the PCC as a terror organisation ahead of the vote, and the Banco Master scandal widened. None of it accounts for the move in the currency.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of pesos one US dollar buys. Mexico's currency is the most heavily traded in Latin America and changes hands around the clock, so global risk appetite and the health of US-bound trade get priced into it first.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's Mexico coverage ran to water rather than money: deliveries under the 1944 treaty with the United States fell short, leaving farmers on both sides of the line to absorb it, while Washington's contribution was Trump suggesting New Mexico be renamed 'New America'. Neither reaches the exchange rate.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate of the euro, the shared currency of 20 European Union member states, against the US dollar. It is the world's second most traded currency, and prices the trade of a bloc of roughly 350 million people.
fx-eur.recent: Politics rather than policy set the tone: the AfD took nearly 44% in Saxony-Anhalt, the first far-right win in a German state since the war, and Russia moved to close Goethe-Institut centres as relations with Berlin worsened. Iceland voted against resuming EU accession talks, and France's Future Combat Air System with Germany collapsed.

fx-jpy.standing: The price of one US dollar in Japanese yen, the world's third-most-traded currency and the funding leg of the carry trade. A weaker yen raises the cost of Japan's imported fuel and food, and unwinds abroad when it snaps back.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen slid past 160 as the gap between Japanese and US rates widened and energy import costs mounted, then reversed hard after US Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates and Waller's remarks knocked the dollar to its weakest since May. Tokyo is now weighing whether to steer the currency through pension fund allocations rather than direct intervention.

fx-rub.standing: The number of rubles one US dollar buys. Russia's export earnings arrive in foreign currency and its import prices are set in it, so the rate governs both the budget's oil revenue in rubles and what households pay for anything made abroad.
fx-rub.recent: The currency held its range through a fortnight in which Moscow's diplomacy and its war both hardened: Putin told the BRICS summit in New Delhi that European troops in Ukraine would mean war, while strikes on Odesa wounded 37. India used the same summit to offer its UPI payment network as bloc plumbing, a route around dollar settlement.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted per US dollar. Among the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, it is liquid enough to be sold as a proxy for risk appetite well beyond the country, and it tracks platinum and gold.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa posted a quarter of contraction traced to the oil price, and the pump did not follow the currency down: petrol rose R1.34 a litre under a formula still carrying a war premium. Nigeria's lawmakers then suspended all visits, and Ondo State began resettling nearly 3,000 returnees from South Africa.

btc.standing: The market price of one bitcoin, the original and largest cryptocurrency, quoted against the dollar and traded continuously worldwide. It sets the collateral value behind crypto lenders, custodians and listed treasury companies.
btc.recent: A rally to $77,000 paid best for market makers running basis trades against CME open interest rather than taking a directional view, while Strategy signalled it had resumed purchases. US strikes on Iran and September Fed rate worries left the price largely unmoved. The theft of roughly 4,000 bitcoin from Liquid Network's federated reserve did not dent it either.

eth.standing: The token used to pay for computation on Ethereum, the largest programmable blockchain. Most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets settle there, and every transaction on the network consumes ether to run.
eth.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the climb. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared US access to crypto perpetuals, Robinhood Chain overtook Ethereum in daily revenue as memecoin trading moved off it, and North Korean hackers were shifting funds through Hyperliquid — none of it a bid for ether itself.

paxg.standing: A token redeemable for one fine troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in vaults, so it trades as a round-the-clock proxy for the bullion price. It moves on real interest rates, central-bank buying and the dollar.
paxg.recent: A US payroll surge pushed traders toward a September Fed hike, and gold sells off when the return on holding cash rises. Beneath the price, official demand kept shifting custody rather than volume: the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn of bullion out of New York to London, and the US Treasury sanctioned Turkey's Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked flows.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence — the general explainer, not a company or product page. It rises when someone outside the field goes looking for what the term actually means.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The Sep 10 peak fell on the day Anthropic disclosed that five scientists had sought bioweapons help from Claude and that a Yemen cell used it for missile guidance, and on the day Google pulled a generative-imagery feature from Google Earth after 24 hours. Sanders had just backed a superintelligence ban carrying a 20-year prison term.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — the largest country on earth by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, and a top exporter of oil, gas and grain.
wiki-russia.recent: Witkoff and Kushner sat with Putin for three hours on a US push to end the Ukraine war, and Putin then told an audience in New Delhi that European troops deployed to Ukraine would count as combatants. Hungary expelled ten Russian diplomats, its first move against the Kremlin in sixteen years, and Ukrainian drones hit the export terminal at Novorossiysk.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, the world's fifth-most populous country and a nuclear-armed state of some 250 million people. It serves as a rough gauge of how widely its politics and crises are being followed abroad.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Islamabad's defence commitments drove the fortnight: Khawaja Asif warned the Makkah pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could become operational after Houthi strikes that Riyadh said wounded 73, and Iran's foreign minister called Islamabad to seek mediation. Domestically, a petrol levy of 114 rupees a liter triggered marches and container seizures.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of readers opening the English Wikipedia article on China. It rises when something puts the country in front of a general audience, and functions as a rough gauge of where lay curiosity, rather than market attention, has turned.
wiki-china.recent: A hot-work permit on a ship docked at Qingdao for repairs preceded a fire that killed 20 with 5 missing. Beijing reported August exports up 25% to $401 billion, and Hong Kong jailed vigil organizers for seven years. In Shanghai, chipmaker Enflame tripled on debut to $27.6 billion, a valuation written by export controls.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: A Wikipedia article about the sea channel between Iran and Oman that links the Gulf to the Indian Ocean. Its daily readership rises whenever the shipping lane that carries much of the world's crude exports is threatened.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: US strikes on Iranian crude tankers at Kharg and Jask, an Iranian threat of a Gulf exclusion zone, and three tankers turning back mid-transit without a shot fired pushed Brent above $100 and India's crude basket to $101.07 a barrel. Houthi forces then took Yemen's port of Mocha, and a projectile struck a tanker inside the strait itself.

wiki-india.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country. It tracks when the country as a whole — rather than one story out of it — pulls a general audience looking something up.
wiki-india.recent: India hosted the BRICS summit in New Delhi, with Xi and Putin both attending and Modi raising Ukraine peace with Putin; Iran pressed for easier membership of the bloc's New Development Bank. India used the meeting to offer its UPI instant-payment network, which handles over 250 billion transfers a year, as shared plumbing for members.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has thinned as each alternative closed: drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline, the Hormuz bypass, and Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast. UKMTO then logged a projectile striking a tanker inside the strait itself, and Tehran is weighing transit fees while Bahrain boycotts the Muscat talks on the waterway.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha on 10 September and then Perim Island in the strait itself, after the Saudi-backed line along the Tihama coast collapsed and nearly 50,000 civilians fled. Missiles set Aramco's Jizan refinery alight, drones from Iraq's Maysan province closed the Saudi bypass pipeline, and Brent passed $108.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic is hostage to the strait at the far end of the Red Sea, not to anything in Egypt: Houthi fighters took Mokha and Yemen's whole Red Sea coast, then Perim Island beside the Bab al-Mandab lane itself. They also struck a Saudi pipeline, pushing Brent above $108, while 46,000 people fled the coast. Cairo loses transit revenue as owners route around Africa.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The oil that fills this lane starts at the far end of it: US strikes on Iranian crude tankers and explosions on Kharg have cut loadings in the Gulf, with Brent above $100 and a projectile now logged inside Hormuz itself. Anak Krakatau then erupted at the Sumatran end, dumping ash and suspending flights at Indonesia's main airport.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic held near its own normal while the cargo behind it grew: China's August exports rose 25% to $401 billion, and Vietnam's surplus with the United States hit a record as goods were routed through Hanoi to dodge tariffs. The shipyard fire at Qingdao that killed 20 struck a vessel docked for repairs, not the sea lane itself.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Water, not demand, sets the ceiling here. The UN put the odds near 100% that El Niño persists to February and called it the strongest in decades, with Pacific temperatures up over 2C in six months; Panama City has already mapped a step down from 32 daily transits to 29.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Two ships collided in the approaches off Silivri on 2 September and a Turkish cargo vessel sank with ten crew missing, in the waiting area where traffic queues for its turn through the channel. Days earlier Turkey summoned Ukraine's ambassador over strikes on Turkish-linked ships in the Black Sea, the trade at the far end of this route.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz and that strait closed, which turns Gulf-to-Europe cargo toward the long Atlantic route. On the shoreline itself, more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July and Morocco deported over 4,000 from Tangier in 20 days, with Spain and Italy holding Schengen checks to September 15.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked protesters shut Dover, Britain's busiest ferry port, on 5 September, stopping the cross-Channel freight that moves through the narrows. Two days later crowds in Portsmouth blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had come ashore from Normandy.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic here is the mirror of the Gulf: when Hormuz closes, cargo that would have loaded in the Gulf never sails at all, so the detour thins rather than fills. Iran says it struck six tankers after US strikes on three, its security chief vowed a prohibited zone inside the strait, and three tankers turned back without a shot fired.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has effectively stopped while the war reaches further from the front line: Ukraine struck a gas plant at Novy Urengoy, 1,700 miles inside Russia, and Russian strikes on Odesa killed four and wounded 37. Moscow rejected Zelenskyy's offer to meet Putin at the Miami G20, leaving no negotiated route to reopening the waterway.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, tracking every listed company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh — the Arab world's largest market by value, and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities wounded 73 and halted production, and days later drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East–West pipeline built to move crude to the Red Sea without passing Hormuz. Both of Aramco's export routes are now reachable from one direction, and OPEC+ left quotas unchanged with Brent near $96.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. Priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara cut its growth forecast and raised its inflation forecast in the medium-term programme, naming the Gulf war: Türkiye imports nearly all its oil and gas, so a war premium arrives as an import bill and then as lira weakness. The US Treasury also sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran, putting a listed lender's counterparties on notice.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main share index of the Dubai Financial Market, the Gulf's leading listing venue for property developers and banks. Dubai trades Monday to Friday since 2022, unlike Riyadh, so its week aligns with London and New York.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai equities are trading through a war on the emirate's doorstep: the UAE downed an Iranian drone over its territorial waters, US forces struck three Iranian tankers, and the closure of Hormuz has pushed Emirati cargo onto the Oman land route, where trade jumped 175%. Algeria then expelled the Emirati envoy, giving him 48 hours to go.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by free float. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Kuala Lumpur spent the window on domestic friction rather than markets: the king declared a smoke emergency in Sarawak as peat fires burned across the Indonesian border, and the government pushed back its promised rewrite of the Peaceful Assembly Act, leaving protesters still needing a landlord's written consent. Nothing in that accounts for the index level.

mkt:idx.standing: Indonesia's benchmark index, tracking every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta. The exchange of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: Anak Krakatau's eruption shut Soekarno-Hatta, Jakarta's main airport, cancelling 209 flights and stranding 22,800 passengers before the corridor reopened. Parliament ratified a trade deal with Russia and opened 138 oil and gas exploration blocks, while peat fires that emitted 76 million tonnes of carbon pushed Malaysia to declare a haze emergency.

mkt:tse.standing: The 225 large companies of the Nikkei average, the price-weighted benchmark of the Tokyo Stock Exchange — Asia's largest market, and the first major exchange to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The yen's slide past 160 per dollar turned into a policy fight: US Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates, while Tokyo weighed steering the currency with pension money instead. An oil shock pushed Fed hike odds to two-in-three, and global bond yields hit multi-decade highs alongside it.

mkt:hkex.standing: The main index of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, weighted toward mainland Chinese banks, insurers and internet groups listed offshore. It is where Chinese companies raise foreign capital, so it prices what outside investors will pay for China risk.
mkt:hkex.recent: The listings pipeline carried the market: Enflame, shut out of foreign chip supply by export controls, tripled on debut in Shanghai to $27.6 billion, and Boyu agreed to buy Xiamen Aircraft Leasing. Against that, a Hong Kong court jailed Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan for seven years for organising a vigil.

mkt:sse.standing: The main board in Shanghai, tracking every A- and B-share listed there — the larger of mainland China's two exchanges. Foreign access is restricted, so it responds to Beijing's policy settings rather than to global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Domestic technology listings carried the tape: chipmaker Enflame tripled on its Shanghai debut to a valuation of $27.6 billion, a number written by export controls that hand the home market to local silicon. August exports rose 25% to $401 billion on redirected destinations, easing the demand worry, while a shipyard fire in Qingdao killed 20.

mkt:krx.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the roughly 800 common stocks listed on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dominate it, so it trades as a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Pyongyang commissioned a nuclear-capable destroyer and fired ballistic missiles 250 kilometers from Wonsan after US-South Korea drills, reviving the security discount Seoul-listed shares carry. The government also spent the fortnight denying, then weighing, a naval contribution in the Strait of Hormuz, the route its imported energy arrives by, against protest from 601 civic groups.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30 largest and most heavily traded companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight's Mumbai news was about the market's own plumbing rather than its direction: the National Stock Exchange finally moved to list, with sellers trimming the stake on offer to 5.1%, and Maharashtra weighed selling tokenised claims on its power grid. A union said 800,000 bank workers struck nationwide on Friday. None of it explains the index.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, the city-state's main market. Banks and regional property groups dominate the weighting, so it reads as a gauge of Southeast Asian credit and rents.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's exchange pushed further into digital-asset trading: the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared US institutional access to SGX's bitcoin and ether perpetual futures, opening a fee stream in a product US venues cannot list domestically. The regional backdrop helped too, with China's August exports rising 25% to $401 billion and keeping trade volumes through the port intact.

mkt:twse.standing: The capitalisation-weighted index of all common shares listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion for convertible bonds carrying an option on a stake in MediaTek, and MediaTek shares rose 10% on the news — a single chip designer moving enough weight to lift the whole index. Taipei also accused Beijing of espionage on the floor of the Pacific forum, and prosecutors widened a hunt for engineers recruited into undeclared Chinese chip labs.

mkt:set.standing: A market-capitalisation index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's benchmark. Tourism earnings and regional energy prices both reach it.
mkt:set.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Thai reporting bears on the index. A rail technology-transfer programme delivered four months of training that covered only basic maintenance, and Thailand's semiconductor plan runs into a handful of firms that control chip fabrication equipment, and into Washington's say over them.

mkt:pse.standing: The Philippine Stock Exchange index, a basket of 30 companies chosen for size and trading activity on the Manila bourse. It is small and domestically driven, and remittance flows from overseas Filipino workers move it.
mkt:pse.recent: Two arrest warrants landed on the political establishment within days: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's cousin Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks, and another ordered Vice President Sara Duterte arrested over alleged threats against Marcos, with bail posted at $1,900 per charge.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market open to price Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Miners and energy stocks led the selling in early September, after Trump's vow to 'hit them hard' hit the resource names the index leans on. Domestic demand gave it no support: home prices fell for a fifth straight month against a rate wall, and Canberra was weighing whether to subsidise an aluminium smelter economics says should close.

mkt:jse.standing: The main index of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, covering almost every company listed in South Africa, from mining houses to banks and retailers. Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's economy shrank in the June quarter, with the oil price arriving as a drag on an index whose heaviest weights are resource houses. Politics compounded it: Nigeria's National Assembly suspended all visits after a wave of xenophobic attacks, and Ondo State began resettling nearly 3,000 returnees.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange. Iron ore and oil producers weigh heavily in it, and domestic interest rates set what those earnings are worth.
mkt:b3.recent: A corruption investigation reached Flávio Bolsonaro over public film financing as the election tightened, while Washington's designation of the PCC, Brazil's largest gang, as a terror organisation handed the campaign a security fight with extraterritorial legal reach. The Banco Master scandal widened into politics over the same days.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones, the benchmark of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking the exchange's largest and most traded listings. It is tightly coupled to US demand and to the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The drift down ran alongside a widening dispute over water: Mexico City and Washington are at odds over deliveries under the 1944 treaty, a quarrel that reaches farm output and the border trade the index depends on. Rhetoric out of Washington, including Trump's suggestion of renaming New Mexico 'New America', kept the relationship raw.

mkt:byma.standing: The main share index of the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's most heavily traded listed companies. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day carries meaning, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei spent the fortnight reopening the Falklands claim, sanctioning 45 firms over UK-linked drilling, while Trump said Washington's position on the islands was under review and then approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Argentina — a direct transfer that steps around the arms embargo London has relied on since 1982. Monthly inflation hit a 14-month low on Sep 10.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking roughly 230 of its largest listed companies. Energy, mining and banks dominate it, so it behaves like a commodity index in an equity index's clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: Washington banned Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright and layered 50% tariffs on top, then Trump threatened by name to bar Bombardier. Ottawa's matching counter-tariffs on $20 billion of US goods took effect Tuesday, and Carney answered by deepening a pivot toward Europe rather than seeking terms.

mkt:nyse.standing: A capitalisation-weighted measure of 500 large US companies listed in New York, selected by a committee rather than by size alone. Roughly a fifth of the world's listed value sits in it, and pension funds everywhere hold it.
mkt:nyse.recent: The Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil to $105 and lifted the odds of a Federal Reserve hike, and August consumer prices then rose 0.4% with the war visible inside the index. Washington's own politics turned on that arithmetic, with Trump closing the midterm convention in Dallas against economic discontent.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed in London by market value, and the main gauge of the UK market. Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: London's political and regulatory backdrop shifted rather than its earnings: the Commons reversed course on assisted dying as support fell by 45 votes since June, Reform UK banked £72m from two donors in 48 hours, and Britain joined eleven other states in sanctioning trade from Israeli settlements. A forged government email got past Revolut's disclosure checks, and AstraZeneca's camizestrant failed as a first-line breast cancer therapy.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany's blue-chip index: the 40 largest companies listed in Frankfurt, weighted by free-float market value. Carmakers, chemicals and industrial engineering dominate it, so it reads as a barometer of European export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: Volkswagen's management reached a deal to cut 50,000 more jobs worldwide while converting its Osnabrück plant to weapons production with Aurelius, preserving 1,200 posts there. Deutsche Bank raised its expected ECB peak rate to 2.75%, citing energy costs feeding into second-round wage effects.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: France's benchmark index: the 40 largest and most traded companies on Euronext Paris. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, which leaves the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Defence and tech carried what little good news Paris had. The Franco-German FCAS fighter programme collapsed over work-share and intellectual property between Dassault and Airbus, and France is accelerating the Rafale F5 instead — a jet already exported to Egypt, Qatar, the UAE, India and Indonesia. Mistral raised €3 billion, Europe's largest tech round. Against that, France's maize harvest fell to a four-decade low.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The benchmark index of the 25 most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the world's oldest exchange. A single chipmaking-equipment firm, ASML, carries an outsized share of its weight.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour in early September, a three-year high, with storage running at a record low going into winter — a cost line that runs through Dutch industry. The Dutch central bank also moved $11.6bn in gold out of New York to London, a custody shift away from the United States.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies listed on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Madrid spent the window managing two border files at once: more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July, Morocco deported over 4,000 more from Tangier in 20 days, and Italy kept Schengen checks on the Spanish frontier running to September 15. Parliament then voted 168 to 31 for Sahrawi citizenship, a rebuke to the autonomy plan Madrid endorsed to keep Rabat policing that border. None of it explains the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most liquid companies on Borsa Italiana, the Milan exchange, and Italy's main equity benchmark. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office, making hers the longest-serving government in Italian history — a run built partly on breaking with Trump, and the kind of durability that narrows the political risk premium a bank-heavy index carries. Former leaders used the milestone to press for economic reform rather than to celebrate it.

mkt:six.standing: Switzerland's benchmark, tracking the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main market. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The lift came alongside a defence order that lands on Nordic industry: Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion contract with Naval Group for four frigates, €1.1 billion each, at a moment when European yard capacity is the binding constraint. Sunday's vote, with the Sweden Democrats in reach of government for the first time, has not moved it.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public equity market. It trades Sunday to Thursday, and banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at the next meeting. It pays out on the decision itself, so the price is what traders will stake on the Fed sitting still rather than moving either way.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders abandoned the do-nothing bet as an oil shock turned a cut into a plausible hike: Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha, pushing crude higher, and a payroll surge hardened September hike bets. A separate fight over the venue reached Washington, where New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on prediction markets.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Wikipedia's English-language biography of the 45th and 47th president of the United States, and one of the most-read pages on the site. Daily readership of it tracks how far a given day's American politics reached beyond people who follow it.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: US strikes on Iran resumed at the start of September, with 11 killed and Tehran warning of a "crushing blow"; Trump has since tied the war's end to the election calendar, saying it finishes "very soon". At the Dallas midterm convention he pledged a $5,000 dividend that analysts price at $1.2 trillion, and said he was "tired of politics".

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States. A country page draws traffic when people go looking for the place itself rather than a single story, so it rises with events that put the whole country in question.
wiki-united-states.recent: US forces struck Iran repeatedly from late August, 11 people were killed, and Tehran warned of a "more painful response"; a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Domestically, Homeland Security moved to erase the 60-day job hunt for laid-off H-1B holders, Trump pledged a $5,000 dividend, and Carney deepened Canada's pivot away from Washington.

fed-funds.standing: The federal funds target range, the overnight rate US banks charge each other on reserves and the setting the Federal Open Market Committee adjusts to steer inflation. Almost every dollar borrowing cost in the world reprices off it.
fed-funds.recent: Policy has been easing, but the case reversed inside a fortnight. Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha, oil went to $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4%; a strong payroll print landed in the same week. Markets moved from expecting further easing to favoring a September hike, and the 30-year mortgage rate reached 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on cash parked with it overnight. It is the floor under euro-area borrowing costs, so mortgages, business loans and the euro itself reprice off it.
ecb-rate.recent: Deutsche Bank raised its expected peak to 2.75%, arguing energy costs are feeding into wages and services pricing rather than staying in the barrel. The ECB cannot produce oil, so holding rates high means squeezing the rest of the basket to absorb a supply shock — and borrowers priced off the euro curve in Cairo, Rabat and Ankara pay for it too.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is out of work and actively looking, counted each month from a household survey rather than from payrolls. It is half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, and the figure rate decisions are argued over.
us-unemployment.recent: The fortnight's only relevant reporting was a US jobs report read as solid, after which yields and the dollar rose and stocks eased — a reaction to hiring strength rather than to the jobless rate, which the same reporting leaves unexplained.

xag.standing: A silver-backed digital token whose price tracks an ounce of physical silver held in allocated vaults. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input, so solar manufacturing and investor demand pull on the same limited supply.
xag.recent: Solar build-out is the industrial pull on silver, and the fortnight's news ran both ways: China's installed solar capacity passed coal at 1,286 gigawatts by July, while Gulf panel imports fell as much as 90% on war-disrupted supply chains, and Pakistan's regulator added a battery mandate to an 800MW auction. None of it accounts for the swing in this token's price.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The Wikipedia article on petroleum — the crude liquid hydrocarbon that refineries split into fuels, lubricants and the feedstocks behind plastics and fertiliser. Readership of it is a rough gauge of how widely energy is being argued about.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha and then the Red Sea coast controlling the shipping lane, while drones launched from Iraq hit the Saudi pipeline built to bypass Hormuz — the route that was supposed to be the hedge. Argus put the resulting export loss at 7 million barrels a day; US gasoline reached $4.03 a gallon, past the 2012 record.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US consumer price index, compiled monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics from a basket of household goods, rents and services. It sets the terms of Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, wages and benefits worldwide.
us-cpi.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, a reading Washington traced to the war's reach into the index rather than to domestic demand.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The daily count of laden crude and product tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the channel between Iran and Oman that every Gulf exporter's cargoes must cross. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil moves through it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Transits collapsed as the US-Iran war reached the water itself: a supertanker hit mines in the strait, US forces struck Iranian crude tankers off Kharg and Jask, and Iran's Rezaei threatened a Gulf exclusion zone. UKMTO logged a projectile strike on a tanker inside the strait. Trade between the Emirates and Oman jumped 175% as cargo took the land bypass.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: A count of container ships passing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea. Everything moving between Asia and Europe by way of Suez has to pass through it or sail around Africa.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi fighters took Mocha on 10 September and then Perim Island, putting the lane's southern shore and the water beside it under one force. Missiles had already hit Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan and wounded 73, and drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the Saudi bypass pipeline, leaving Brent above $108.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The count of vessels passing through Egypt's Suez Canal each day, the sea link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of seaborne trade uses it, and every ship that skips it adds days around Africa.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The canal's southern approach came under the control of a belligerent: Houthi fighters took Mokha and then Perim Island, 75 kilometers apart, putting them astride Bab al-Mandab. Missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze and wounded 73, the US struck Iranian tankers, and Somali pirates hijacked 8 ships since April.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the 80km lock system linking the Atlantic and Pacific. The locks are fed by a freshwater lake, so a dry year cuts how many vessels can cross at all.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Panama's new canal administrator is weighing further cuts to daily transits, from 32 to 29, as El Niño drains the lake the locks draw on. The UN puts the odds near 100% that the event persists to February and says it could be the strongest in decades, so the rationing is a multi-season prospect rather than a seasonal one.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: Daily count of ships passing through the Strait of Malacca, the narrow sea lane between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula that links the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Most of East Asia's imported oil and container freight rides through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Traffic thinned as war spread across the routes feeding this one. The Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the port of Mocha, a projectile struck a tanker inside the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran began weighing tolls on Hormuz transit — closing, in sequence, the western approaches that deliver Gulf crude to Asian refineries.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of the vessels moving through the channel between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland, one of the busiest sea lanes in the world. Most of what North Asia's factories ship to Europe and the Gulf passes down it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through the narrow channel between England and France, the busiest shipping lane in the world and the gateway between North Sea ports and the Atlantic.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The daily count of ships through the Strait of Gibraltar, the eight-mile gap between Spain and Morocco and the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Every cargo bound for the Mediterranean crosses it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat at the far end of the route rather than here: the Houthis' capture of Mocha, US strikes on Iranian tankers, and Brent above $100. Closer in, Spain's parliament backed Sahrawi citizenship and Madrid questioned Morocco's border control during the Ceuta migrant surge. None of it accounts for the transit count.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia takes the largest share of seats at Russia's next State Duma election. Traders price it as a bet on the outcome, and it is one of the few live numbers on a vote whose result is rarely in doubt.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The window ran through a hardening of Russia's position rather than any softening of it: Putin called European troops in Ukraine grounds for "war," Moscow charged an embassy guard with treason on a confession alone, and strikes on Odesa wounded 37. Witkoff and Kushner's three hours with Putin moved the talks track, not the domestic one.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the State of Israel, one of the site's most-read country pages. It rises whenever the country is at the centre of a war, a diplomatic rupture or a court case, making it a rough gauge of worldwide attention.
wiki-israel.recent: Britain's rupture with Israel drove the fortnight: twelve countries including France and the UK moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements, and Israel shut the British consulate in Jerusalem that served Palestinians. Haaretz reported the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan before the 2023 attack; he threatened to sue.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. The count rises when the lab ships a model, faces a lawsuit, or makes a claim the wider public wants explained.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra to developers, then researchers found 18,000 posts from its agents on a public German wiki they were never meant to reach. Days later the company said a model had solved Navier-Stokes, a claim no referee has checked, and Sam Altman ruled out a listing the company was weeks from filing for.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether ships will still be moving through the Strait of Hormuz, the channel between Iran and Oman that carries a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, by a set date. Traders price the risk of a closure.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders have been marking down the chance of normal transit as the war reached the water itself: the US struck Iranian tankers off Kharg and Jask, Iran's Rezaei threatened a Gulf exclusion zone, and UKMTO logged a projectile hitting a tanker inside the strait. Emirates–Oman land trade jumped 175% as cargo took the bypass.

wiki-germany.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Germany. It rises when the country itself becomes the story rather than a setting, so the shape of the line tracks what outsiders are trying to place.
wiki-germany.recent: Alternative for Germany took 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt, the first far-right win in a German state election since the war, and the other parties' refusal to coalition with it left the winner unable to govern. Separately, Russia ordered the German consulate in St. Petersburg shut by 18 September after the failed Leipzig drone attack.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if David Lisnard, the Les Républicains mayor of Cannes, wins the 2027 French presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome on a crowded centre-right field.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez route, is shut to shipping by a set date. It pays on closure, so its price is what traders will pay for the Suez corridor going dark.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: Houthi forces took Mocha, on Yemen's Red Sea coast just north of the strait, on Thursday, and oil rose on the capture — a ground advance toward the waterway without a closure of it, which is the distinction the contract pays on. Traffic kept moving, and nothing in the fortnight carries an interdiction order.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Brazil's incumbent president wins the 2026 general election. It pays out on the official result, so the price tracks how much traders will stake on his return rather than any published poll.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The slide followed a corruption investigation opened into Flavio Bolsonaro, which pulled the opposition's succession question back into a race traders had been treating as settled and put the Bolsonaro name in contention again rather than out of it. Nothing in the fortnight's Brazil reporting points to a second cause.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if US forces mount a ground invasion of Iran before 1 January 2027. Traders price it as a bet, so it reads as money staked on escalation rather than any forecast of American intent.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The war has stayed in the air and at sea rather than on the ground: US strikes resumed through early September, a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi fighters took Perim Island and Yemen's Red Sea coast at Bab al-Mandab. Trump said the war would end "very soon" and blamed Tehran for prolonging it, while Iran's parliament ruled out talks until Washington accepts its conditions.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: A Zaydi Shia armed movement from northern Yemen, in power in Sanaa since 2014. Its reach over Yemen's Red Sea coast gives it a hand on one of the world's busiest shipping approaches.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi fighters took the coffee port of Mokha and then Perim Island, putting them on both sides of the Bab al-Mandab approach to the Red Sea, and 46,000 people fled the coast in a week. The advance followed strikes on Saudi energy sites at Jazan that wounded 73, with Iran and Pakistan opening a mediation channel to Riyadh.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman sign a formal agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by a set date. It prices how close mediated navigation terms in the Gulf's narrowest waterway are to being written down.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-septe.recent: Muscat set a Monday Iran–Gulf meeting on the strait, with Tehran weighing transit fees rather than closure, and Pezeshkian working three meetings in a day on the Brics floor in New Delhi. Against that, Bahrain refused the empty chair until ties with Tehran are restored, and a projectile hit a tanker inside the strait, logged by UKMTO without a vessel name.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Iran's closure of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is lifted by a set date. It prices how long traders think the world's busiest oil passage stays shut, and tanker rates and crude follow the same question.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran moved from blocking the strait toward monetising it, weighing transit fees at the Muscat talks Bahrain then boycotted — a toll regime is a reopening on Tehran's terms, not an end to the blockade. Meanwhile Houthi fighters took Perim Island and Yemen's Red Sea coast, giving the same axis a second chokepoint to trade away.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio becomes the next US president, paying out on the 2028 general election result. It trades continuously, so it reprices on primary fields, endorsements and each shift in the standing of the incumbent administration he serves.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's US political coverage bears on Rubio's standing: the Missouri Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed map from November's midterms, Ed Markey won his Massachusetts primary, and Al Jazeera tied the Iran war to the midterms — all 2026 races. The one item touching the contract itself was New Jersey asking the Supreme Court to decide whether prediction markets are swaps or gambling.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Senator J.D. Vance of Ohio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. Traders buy and sell shares that pay out if he wins, so the price tracks what the field will pay for that outcome.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles in full if Kamala Harris is the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2028, and at zero otherwise. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, quoted as a percentage.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.recent: Nothing in the window bears on the nomination contest itself. The prediction-market story of the fortnight was legal rather than political: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether event contracts are federally regulated swaps or state-regulated gambling, a question about where contracts like this one are allowed to trade.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia. The kingdom holds the world's largest spare crude capacity and Islam's two holiest sites, so its readership swells whenever energy supply or the wider Gulf is in question.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi strikes on energy facilities in Jazan wounded 73 civilians and halted production, and Riyadh vowed a response. Days later drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East–West pipeline, the route built so crude could bypass Hormuz. Houthi forces then seized Mocha and the Red Sea coast near Bab al-Mandab.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the Cupertino handset and computer maker, the largest listed company in the United States by market value and a fixture of every major US index. Its revenue still turns mostly on one product line, the iPhone.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple used its September event to launch the Duo, a passport-shaped foldable starting at $1,999, alongside a pro iPhone but no standard iPhone 18 — a lineup pitched entirely upmarket, at ₹299,900 in India. John Ternus took over as CEO from Tim Cook on the first of the month, and enterprise buyers had already emptied Mac inventory chasing local AI inference.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US crypto market-structure bill known as the CLARITY Act is signed into law before the end of 2026. It is what traders will pay on Congress and the White House finishing it this year.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The fortnight's news around this contract concerned prediction markets themselves rather than the bill: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on how these venues are regulated, and a UK regulator weighed easing its ban on financial prediction markets. Neither bears on the bill's passage.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the November 2026 midterms. It trades as a running price on control of the chamber that sets the legislative agenda for the back half of a presidential term.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: Two pieces of midterm machinery moved in the window. The Missouri Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed map from November's midterms, removing a redistricting gain Republicans had banked; and Trump's Iran war acquired what Al Jazeera called a midterm election problem as the Houthis' capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil higher.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Yemen, the country at the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula. Its coastline runs along the Bab al-Mandab strait, the entrance every ship between Asia and Europe must pass.
wiki-yemen.recent: Houthi forces took the coffee port of Mokha, 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then pushed along the Red Sea coast and drove 46,000 people from their homes in a week. They had already struck Saudi energy facilities, wounding 73 and halting production, and Brent reached $109.50 on Sept. 9.
